crypto_weaknesses_justification: Maintained standard cryptography is used in the owned supported profile; a complete review of all external coordinator firmware, Home Assistant and release-runtime algorithms against this broader weakness criterion is not established. https://github.com/ha-homelab/slzb-06-recovery/blob/main/docs/security-design.md
crypto_keylength_justification: SLZB_TLS_SECURITY_LEVEL=3 reaches all owned urllib/aiohttp HTTPS/WSS paths and rejects weaker-than-128-bit estimated keys (RSA/DH3072, EC256), while preserving certificate/hostname checks. Real TLS1.2/1.3 tests reject 2047-bit leaf/intermediate/root keys before data. The documented release-client configuration uses gh2.102.0/Go1.27.1 with GODEBUG=fips140=on to filter complete verified chains. Legacy coordinator plaintext protocols are not claimed encrypted. https://github.com/ha-homelab/slzb-06-recovery/blob/main/docs/security-design.md
crypto_pfs_justification: Forward secrecy across every supported external runtime and peer has not been established; no complete deployment-wide claim is made. https://github.com/ha-homelab/slzb-06-recovery/blob/main/docs/security-design.md
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project does not create or store external-user password verifiers. Operator-provided Home Assistant tokens are machine credentials used to access an existing external service. https://github.com/ha-homelab/slzb-06-recovery/blob/main/docs/security-design.md
crypto_random_justification: The host tools use Python/OpenSSL and aiohttp for verified TLS, standard hashlib SHA-256 for pinned firmware/integrity, and os.urandom for multipart identifiers. Release transport/signing delegates to maintained GitHub CLI and Sigstore tools. TLS/key generation uses the maintained implementation’s cryptographically secure randomness, not Python random. https://github.com/ha-homelab/slzb-06-recovery/blob/main/docs/security-design.md
